body:
## Question

Does the IONOS AI Model Hub fit as the Operator-set LLM endpoint: models offered (text and image input), OpenAI-compatible API and its gaps, schema-constrained output (`response_format` `json_schema`), context sizes, price per token, rate limits and quotas, where inference runs, what is logged or kept, terms on processing personal data? Compare with the needs in the public repo's `docs/research/llm-item-extraction.md`.

comments.body:
**Resolution:** The IONOS AI Model Hub fits as the Operator-set LLM endpoint, with two things to measure and one to clear on paper. No blocker found.

- API: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/models` at `https://openai.inference.de-txl.ionos.com/v1` (Berlin only). `response_format` `json_schema`/`strict` is in the schema but "model-specific"; documented by example only for Llama 3.3 70B. Measure.
- Adapter gap: it always sends `reasoning_effort: "low"`; IONOS rejects unsupported values. Documented as accepted only by Qwen3.8 27B and GPT-OSS 120B. Measure the others; a rejecting model needs a public adapter change.
- Models: 6 LLMs, 128k-262k context; image input on Qwen3.5 9B, Mistral Small 24B, Qwen3.8 27B, Qwen3.5 397B (the adapter sends text only today).
- Price (net, per 1M tokens in/out): 0.10/0.15 EUR (Qwen3.5 9B) to 0.60/3.60 EUR; roughly 0.1-1 EUR per Family and month (own estimate).
- Limits: 5 req/s per model per contract, no token quota documented; 529 load shedding exists; SLA 99.9 %.
- Data: inference only in Germany; prompts/outputs not logged, stored or used for training; metadata (time, model, tokens) kept for an unpublished period; sub-processors only IONOS group (DE, RO, ES); DPA part of the contract.
- Terms: AI terms call script-driven use and making the service available to third parties misuse unless the service description provides otherwise; get written confirmation from IONOS that a multi-tenant SaaS backend is intended use.
- Measure first: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `mistralai/Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct`.

body:
## Question

Can IONOS managed PostgreSQL hold one database and role per Family (about 100 at start, up to about 1000) plus the control database: creating and dropping databases and roles over SQL or API, connection limits per size, versions and upgrade policy, backups and point-in-time recovery, private access from compute, high availability, price per size? Can IONOS Object Storage hold blobs with a prefix per Family: S3 compatibility gaps, scoped access keys, lifecycle rules, versioning, encryption, German regions, price?

comments.body:
Resolved: no blocker found for IONOS (documentation reading only, nothing run on a real contract).

- PostgreSQL (DBaaS v2, Berlin/Frankfurt): the API manages clusters only; per-Family databases and roles are created and dropped with SQL. No limit on their number is documented.
- Hard ceiling: `max_connections` is fixed by RAM, at most 1000 per cluster (989 usable), so about 490–989 concurrently active Families per cluster. The managed PgBouncer pools per database and role and does not lift this.
- Backups: daily base backup + WAL every 5 minutes, retention 1–365 days, point-in-time restore of the whole cluster only; restoring one Family goes through a temporary cluster.
- Access only through an IONOS private LAN; HA with 1–5 instances and automatic failover, 3 recommended.
- Price per 30 days at 2 cores / 8 GB / 100 GB: about €142 for one instance, €425 for three.
- Object Storage (Frankfurt/Berlin): bucket policy, per-prefix lifecycle, versioning, SSE-S3; no IAM or STS, so one service key and prefix isolation in the app. €0.007 per GB per 30 days, requests free.
- To test hands-on before #55: rights of the cluster's initial user (create/drop role and database, revoke connect) and the pooler with SQL-created roles.

Details and open points: `docs/research/ionos-postgres-object-storage.md`

body:
## Question

Which IONOS products can run the public image as `api`, `worker` and `cleanup` workloads plus self-run helpers (OpenBao, Authentik) in a German region: Managed Kubernetes, Cloud Cubes / VPS, Compute Engine servers, any container service? For each: smallest sensible setup and monthly price, scaling and rolling updates, load balancer and public IPs, private networking, container registry, what the Operator must maintain alone (OS patches, cluster upgrades), known limits.

comments.body:
Resolution (prices net, IONOS price list v2026-10-29, 730 h/month):

- No blocker. All options run in Germany (Frankfurt, Berlin).
- IONOS has no container service between VMs and Kubernetes. Choice: Managed Kubernetes, or VMs with Docker Compose.
- Managed Kubernetes, public pool, 2 vCPU nodes (2 vCPU / 8 GB): about 100 EUR/month. Control plane free, IONOS replaces nodes weekly (no OS patching), rolling updates and replicas built in. Recommended.
- Cubes + Docker Compose, 2 Basic Cube M: about 40 EUR/month. Operator patches the OS and builds rollout and scaling himself; disk sits on one host.
- vCPU servers: same burden as Cubes at 2 to 3 times the price; VM Auto Scaling is Early Access.
- ionos.de VPS is a separate platform outside IONOS Cloud: not a fit.
- Catches on Kubernetes: `LoadBalancer` service is a static IP on one node, not a real load balancer (failover undocumented, test it); private node pools need NAT Gateway + NLB (about +50 EUR/month); no IPv6.
- Registry: not needed for the public image; Private Container Registry exists (Frankfurt only).

Details, comparison table, sources and open points: `docs/research/ionos-compute.md`

body:
## Destination

Every decision for running the hosted service on IONOS is made (IONOS product per building block, topology, cost per Family, infrastructure as code, Operator backups and recovery), so the build issues under [Run the hosted multi-Family service](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/24) can be implemented. This map plans only; it builds nothing.

## Notes

- Decisions of [Map: Scaling refactorings for hosted family-agenda (Phase 0 + 1)](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/1) and [Map: Public entry point of the hosted service (landing page, registration, billing)](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/32) stand: public image as shared `api`/`worker`/`cleanup` workloads, one database per Family plus a control database, S3 blobs, Family keys wrapped by the Operator key behind `KeyWrapper` (now a key file, not OpenBao), one address, Matrix messengers never hosted, Operator-set LLM endpoint, Stripe, sign-in through Google or Authentik.
- Why IONOS: location in Germany and its LLM offer (AI Model Hub).
- Placement rule: all Family content and the LLM run at IONOS in Germany. EU services that see no Family content are allowed where IONOS has no fit. Stripe and Google sign-in are external anyway.
- Sizing: start for about 100 Families, design with room up to about 1000.
- Operation: the maintainer alone, best effort, no on-call. Prefer managed services over self-run ones and the simplest compute that fits.
- Private repo: nothing of this goes into the public repo.
- Language: English in tickets; domain terms untranslated (public `GLOSSARY.md` plus this repo's). Skills: `grilling` + `domain-modeling` for decisions, `research` for research tickets (findings in `docs/research/`).

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->
- [Research IONOS compute for the three workloads](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/47): no container service between VMs and Kubernetes; Managed Kubernetes (2 nodes, about 100 EUR/month net, free control plane, no OS patching) fits best, Cubes with Docker Compose (about 40 EUR/month) is the cheap self-maintained alternative; its `LoadBalancer` is only a static IP on one node, untested on node loss (see docs/research/ionos-compute.md).
- [Research IONOS managed PostgreSQL and Object Storage](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/48): fits on paper; database and role per Family over SQL only, no documented count limit; at most 989 usable connections per cluster, fixed by RAM; restore and point-in-time recovery for the whole cluster only; reachable only on the IONOS private LAN; Object Storage in Frankfurt and Berlin without scoped keys, so one service key and prefixes enforced by the app (see docs/research/ionos-postgres-object-storage.md).
- [Research IONOS AI Model Hub for Extraction](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/49): fits on paper; OpenAI-compatible, Berlin only, content neither logged nor trained on, 0.10 to 0.65 EUR per 1M input tokens, 5 requests/s per model, no budget per token; to measure: `json_schema` per model and whether `reasoning_effort: "low"` is accepted; candidates Qwen3.8-27B, gpt-oss-120b, Mistral Small 24B; the terms on use for third parties need IONOS's written word (see docs/research/ionos-ai-model-hub.md).
- [Research IONOS platform services around the workloads](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/50): compute, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL clusters, Object Storage, DNS, certificates, logging and monitoring are covered as code (Terraform / OpenTofu); missing are a managed key service (OpenBao self-run, nothing to auto-unseal against) and transactional mail (external EU sender), and the provider cannot manage AI Model Hub, tokens (90 days at most) or databases per Family; about 8 incidents in 6 weeks; certifications do not name DBaaS or the AI Model Hub (see docs/research/ionos-platform-services.md).
- [Research IONOS VPS and a later move to IONOS Cloud](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/63): VPS L+ only about 4 EUR/month cheaper than one Cube, but a second contract (IONOS SE, AVV EU/EEA), Germany not confirmed, 99 % per year, no API, and no migration path to DCD beyond a manual restore; cheapest sensible start is one Cube in DCD with Docker Compose (see docs/research/ionos-vps.md).
- [Open the IONOS account and an AI Model Hub token](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/51): contract 39683376 (Einzelunternehmer); group `ai-model-hub` but no dedicated user yet, token from the main account at `~/.config/ionos/ai-model-hub.token`, expires 2026-11-13; `/v1/models` answers 200 once trailing whitespace is stripped from the token.
- [Measure Extraction on the AI Model Hub](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/53): on synthetic German mail `json_schema` works on every model; only Qwen3.8-27B (no misses, about 3.30 EUR per 1000 messages) and gpt-oss-120b (4 of 58 missed, about 0.40 EUR) accept the adapter's `reasoning_effort: "low"`; Mistral Small rejects it; about 0.12 to 1 EUR per Family and month; real mail not yet measured.
- [Decide compute platform and topology](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/54): cheapest setup for now. One Basic Cube M in `de/fra` with Docker Compose (`api`/`worker`/`cleanup` ×1, Caddy, Postgres as a container on the NVMe), about 22.50 EUR/month, best effort. WAL archiving to Object Storage is mandatory before registration opens. Postgres moves to IONOS managed at about 100 paying Families, a second Cube, or a tight Cube. Growth: vertical, then workers on a second Cube, then `api` behind an ALB; Kubernetes is reconsidered only there.
- [Decide where OpenBao and Authentik run](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/56): no OpenBao, since on one Cube it protects almost nothing. Instead the Operator key is a versioned root-only key file, mounted only into `api`/`worker`/`cleanup`, never in databases or backups, with offline copies in the password manager and on paper (public adapter: [Wrap Family master keys with a versioned Operator key file](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda/issues/357)). Authentik runs on the same Cube with its own database in the same Postgres, single instance, public on its own subdomain, admin paths blocked, admin through an SSH tunnel; it moves in only after the mail sign-in test passes.
- [Choose and register the domain](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/52): `family-agenda.cloud`, registered at IONOS SE 2026-11-13 (expires 2027-11-13), no variants; apex = landing page, `app.` = service, `auth.` = Authentik, mail from `no-reply@`; DNS stays at IONOS SE for now (see the infrastructure decision), certificates by Caddy over HTTP-01.
- [Decide Postgres hosting and cluster capacity](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/55): start only; Postgres 17 container on the Cube, 3 GB limit, `max_connections` 300 (at most 60 open Instances per `api`/`worker` through the existing LRU cap), no limit on Family databases, control, Family and Authentik databases in one instance; everything about the managed service deferred to the move.
- [Decide infrastructure as code and the release procedure](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/58): simplest start, no rollback. Cube, IP, firewall, buckets set up by hand following a runbook; DNS by hand at IONOS SE; `bootstrap.sh` once; secrets in a root-only `.env` (master copy in the password manager); release = pinned image in `compose.yaml` + `deploy.sh` (rsync, pull, up) from the laptop; errors fixed forward, disasters restored from backup; AI Model Hub token rotated by hand every 80 days.
- [Decide Operator backups and disaster recovery](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/59): WAL-G in our own Postgres image, WAL every 5 min plus a daily base backup, encrypted, to a bucket in Berlin, kept 14 days; blobs stay in Frankfurt with versioning (14 days), no copy; config in repo and password manager; loss at most about 5 min, downtime best effort; one restore runbook (Cube, point in time, one Family); bucket loss accepted; restore drill before registration opens.
- [Decide monitoring, alerts and logs](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/64): dead man's switch at Healthchecks.io (EU, pings only). `health` every 5 min (HTTPS, containers, disk/RAM, WAL archive, overdue backlog, token expiry), `backup` within 26 h, `cleanup` per run; alerts by email and push, no on-call; growth triggers in a CSV on the Cube; logs via rotated Docker `json-file`, no central logging.
- [Research EU transactional mail senders](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/66): every hosted candidate has SMTP for Authentik, an API and a DPA; EU-only without a US parent are Scaleway TEM (FR, about 0.55 EUR at 2.5k and 5 EUR at 20k mails/month, content kept 36 h, default cap 10k) and Lettermint (NL, 10 to 25 EUR, 28 d); Brevo and Mailjet are French with US sub-processors, Mailgun and Postmark have US parents; IONOS Mail sends over SMTP but is a mailbox (50 to 500 mails/h, no API, no webhooks, application use unconfirmed), a self-run MTA puts all deliverability on the Operator (see docs/research/eu-transactional-mail.md).
- [Decide the transactional mail sender](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/67): one IONOS Mail Basic 1 mailbox `no-reply@family-agenda.cloud` over `smtp.ionos.de`:465 for both Authentik's codes and `api`'s confirmations, chosen for one contract less and automatic DKIM, not for placement (the AVV promises only EU/EEA); the AGB say nothing about application sending, so it is permitted by omission; failed handovers are counted into the existing `health` alert, DSN bounces are read by hand in the maintainer's mail client (which also satisfies AGB 10.2), no bounce code; successor Scaleway TEM at repeated `450` or more than 300 mails/hour.
- [Decide staging](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/65): no second environment; the maintainer's self-hosted Instance on the home server is the test place, production itself is tested in the window before registration opens, and each release is guarded by `smoke.sh` run from `deploy.sh` (loud failure, no rollback); only release tags `X.Y.Z` reach production, and the maintainer's own Family is the canary.
- [Decide how plugin containers and their Egress Proxies run on the Cube](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/68): one shared container per hosted Source Type (`ics`, `imap`, `webuntis`, matrix not hosted), each with its own Egress Proxy, generated from a cloud-only `plugins.yml`, no memory limits, about 0.8 GB and 6 containers more (about 7 of 8 GB), vertical move to a Memory Cube M as the trigger; the proxy's allowlist request names its Family through a per-call ticket (Family + Source, HMAC) instead of a cross-Family union, so it is scoped per Source — breaking plugin contract 3.0, handed to [Scope an Egress Proxy's allowlist per Source with a per-call ticket (contract 3.0)](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda/issues/358) and a prerequisite for launch.
- [Decide the LLM model and the interim limit per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/57): `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` for every Family, chosen for quality (58/58 Items against gpt-oss-120b's 54/58) at about 1.00 EUR per Family and month, no automatic fallback; no per-Family cap at launch (volume is bounded by a Family's own Sources), instead a spend alert above 250 EUR/month over the IONOS Billing API (corrected from 50 EUR in [Decide the cost model per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/60)) in the `health` cron; a refusing endpoint stays a temporary error, so the worker backoff ([1.3](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/11)) and the overdue-backlog alert are launch conditions; model id in `.env`, switched by hand after a harness run; real mail still to be measured.
- [Decide the cost model per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/60): about **1.25 EUR per Family and month**, flat across scale — ~1.00 EUR of inference plus ~0.20 of infrastructure; fixed cost is ~26 EUR/month at 100 Families (Cube M, IPv4, mailbox, domain, Object Storage; Postgres still a container) and ~178 at 1000 (Memory Cube M plus managed PostgreSQL at 142), so the LLM is 79 to 85 % of the bill and the only line that scales. Acceptable to go on: yes. Load-bearing assumption, written into the growth CSV and checked against the first month of real usage: 300 messages per Family and month. The price must cover about 3× that volume; at the 4.99 EUR gross the Operator has in mind it covers 3.6×, fixed cost is met at ~10 paying Families, and a Family turns cost-negative above ~1100 messages a month. The tail stays uncapped at launch, successor trigger: one Family above 10 EUR of inference in a month.
- [Decide launch readiness](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/71): launch is three stages, not one event — **(a) own Family** (plugin contract 3.0 for `ics`/`imap`/`webuntis`, worker backoff, build issues released and deployed, certificates and DNS, WAL archiving running), **(b) about 5 invited Families by hand** (Authentik mail sign-in under 60 s at three providers, full timed restore drill plus a single-Family restore, Extraction on at least 50 real anonymised messages with no missed Item in a multi-Item message and at least 95 % of dates and times right, AI spend alert live), **(c) registration opens** (capacity check of 120 databases and 60 open Instances instead of a throughput load test, 7-day clean WAL soak, processing agreements with [#62](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/62) blocking only this stage, entry point from [#32](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/32)); every gate's threshold, measured value and proof live in `docs/launch-checklist.md`, and a gate without a measured value is a failed gate.

## Not yet specified

- Mail that carries Family content (digests, reminders with Task titles): neither IONOS Mail nor an EU sender is covered for it by the placement rule, since no IONOS page names a data centre for Mail Basic. Hangs on [Map: Public entry point of the hosted service (landing page, registration, billing)](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/32) deciding whether such mail exists at all.
- Move to IONOS managed PostgreSQL: cluster size and HA, when a second cluster is added and how the register points to it, where the control database lives, pooler, move procedure and downtime (deferred from [Decide Postgres hosting and cluster capacity](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/55)). Before it, run the deferred [Try a Family database lifecycle on IONOS managed PostgreSQL](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/61) (needs a DCD token; checks SQL role/database rights, pooler, storage classes, retention, single-Family restore).
- Infrastructure expansion, when needed: OpenTofu, Cloud DNS with delegation and DNSSEC, SOPS for secrets, deploying from CI, a restore point before each release, a dedicated IONOS user for the token (deferred from [Decide infrastructure as code and the release procedure](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/58)).
- Observability expansion, when needed: IONOS Logging/Monitoring (managed Grafana), dashboards, `api` p95, metrics per Family (deferred from [Decide monitoring, alerts and logs](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/64)).
- A throwaway Cube for one risky change, at a notable number of Families: which changes earn it (move to managed PostgreSQL, Authentik or Postgres major upgrade, ingress or certificate change, backup/restore path, first destructive migration) and what it shares with production (nothing writable; never the backup bucket) (deferred from [Decide staging](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/65)).

## Out of scope

- Per-Family LLM usage accounting and a real quota per Family: needs the `usage` field of every answer and only matters for billing; it goes to the entry-point map, not here (ruled out in [Decide the LLM model and the interim limit per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/57)).
- Landing page, registration, billing, legal texts: [Map: Public entry point of the hosted service (landing page, registration, billing)](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/32).
- Changes to the public codebase: decided in [Map: Scaling refactorings for hosted family-agenda (Phase 0 + 1)](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/1).
- Other cloud providers, unless a research ticket finds a blocker at IONOS; then the destination is redrawn.
- Setting the price: stays in the entry-point map; this map only supplies cost per Family.
- Payment fees (about 0.25 EUR plus 1.5 to 2.9 % per charge) and VAT treatment: part of the price decision in the entry-point map, listed in [Decide the cost model per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/60) only so it is not forgotten there.

## Question

Does Authentik meet the sign-in decided in [Decide registration flow](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/37)? Run it and verify: user created through the API; repeated sign-in by mail link or code with passwords disabled; passkey optional; two replicas allowed under the free licence; mail scanners do not invalidate links. comments.body:
**Answer: Authentik meets the #37 sign-in.** All five checks pass against Authentik 2026.8.5 (unlicensed; 2 server replicas, 1 worker, PostgreSQL, no Redis), so the Ory Kratos + Hydra fallback was not run. Spike, tests and full results: `spikes/authentik-mail-signin/` (README) on branch `claude/implement-45-6b0034`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| User created through the API | Pass: `POST /api/v3/core/users/`, no usable password, no devices |
| Repeated sign-in by mail code or link, passwords disabled | Pass: code flow (first sign-in enrols the mail device in-flow) and link flow, fresh sessions each time |
| Passkey optional | Pass (browser test): not required at first sign-in, can be added later, passkey and mail code both sign in afterwards |
| Two replicas under the free licence | Runs: flows started on one replica finish on the other. Allowed: reading, not tested. No replica counting in code; "multi-instance" on the pricing page is an Enterprise Plus support item; core MIT |
| Mail scanners do not invalidate links | Pass: a "Continue" step guards the link token; prefetch and unconfirmed opens leave it usable; single use after Continue |

**Notes for implementation**
- Validate stage starts the last-used method on its own (sends a code mail, or opens the passkey prompt); the other is one click away.
- Mail device keeps the address it was enrolled with; address change must reset it (per source, untested).

**Not covered, to do before production**
- Stock `default-authentication-flow` (password) still reachable by URL: delete or replace.
- No test that open signups are unreachable.
- No OIDC provider configured: claims and redirect back to the app untested.
- Scanners that click Continue, or run in a real browser; passkey autofill; passkey on the link flow.

body:
## Question

Where do landing page, registration and Customer area run, on what stack, and how do they reach the control database, provisioning and provider webhooks?

comments.body:
## Resolution

**Placement and stack**
- Own Compose service **`site`**, built from a private image in this repo, in the same Compose project and behind the same Caddy. Nothing of it goes into the public image.
- TypeScript on Node, **Hono + htmx**, server-rendered, with the same toolchain and Family Agenda design system as the public app. No static-site generator; landing page and legal texts are pages of `site`.
- A second service, **`billing-worker`**, runs from the same private image with a different start command and has no ingress.

**URL layout (apex `family-agenda.cloud`)**
- `/` is the landing page; legal texts sit under their own paths. `/register/...` is registration, `/account/...` is the Customer area, and `/stripe/webhook` receives Stripe's events. Paths are English.
- `app.` stays purely the public app. `site` uses host-only cookies on the apex, so they never collide with `app.`'s `<Family id>.<token>` cookie.

**Sign-in on the site**
- `site` is its own OIDC client at Google and Authentik and keeps its own session (session rows in the `site` DB). Nothing is shared with `app.`.
- What happens after signing in on the landing page:
  - **Customer** stays on the landing page; the header shows **App** (link to `app.`, which signs in again through the Identity Provider without a prompt) and **Account** (the Customer area).
  - **Family Member who is not the Customer** is sent straight to `app.`.
  - **Person not yet mapped to a Family** continues the registration.
- The app's Payment lock page links to `/account`.

**Data**
- Own **`site` database** with its own role, in the same Postgres and covered by WAL archiving. It holds:
  - registrations in progress,
  - acceptance records (terms version, timestamp, 18+, consumer),
  - Stripe customer and subscription ids per Family, and who is the Customer (`iss`+`sub`),
  - trial-abuse keys (card fingerprint, verified mail),
  - the webhook inbox, the job queue and rate-limit counters.
- The control database holds only what the public register port defines. `site`'s role gets **SELECT on the identity mapping table only**, for the "already mapped person" check.

**Provisioning and lifecycle**
- `billing-worker` alone holds the Operator key file and the privileged DB role (`CREATEDB`). Internet-facing `site` has neither and only enqueues jobs into the `site` DB; `billing-worker` takes them with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
- **Webhook:** `site` checks the signature and stores the event, unique on the event id, then answers 200. `billing-worker` processes events in order:
  - subscription created in trial: provisioning;
  - `past_due` day 7: Payment lock;
  - payment succeeded: unlock;
  - end, withdrawal or chargeback lost: closing.
- The timing of these steps comes from Stripe's retry and cancel settings where possible; our own timers are used only where Stripe sends no event.
- Every register change goes through the public register/provisioning library, never through raw SQL from private code.
- **Periodic jobs in `billing-worker`:**
  - a daily reconcile of Stripe against the register: it re-enqueues what is safe to repeat (provisioning, unlock) and only raises an alert for anything destructive (lock, closing);
  - deletion of abandoned registrations after 30 days;
  - provisioning retries with backoff, then an Operator alert.

**Cancel and withdraw buttons (§ 312k, withdrawal)**
- Both are public `site` pages, reachable without signing in: identifying data, then a confirmation mail with a link. Both are also offered inside `/account`. Their effects become jobs for `billing-worker`, which acts through the Stripe API.

**Abuse limits**
- Per-IP rate limits live in `site`, with counters in the `site` DB and the client IP from Caddy's `X-Forwarded-For`; the stock Caddy image stays.
- The daily provisioning cap is enforced again in `billing-worker` before `CREATE DATABASE`.

**Mail, release, monitoring**
- `site` and `billing-worker` send through the existing `no-reply@` IONOS mailbox; failed sends are counted into the `health` alert.
- The private image is pinned in `compose.yaml` next to the public one and shipped by `deploy.sh`. `smoke.sh` also covers the apex and `/stripe/webhook`, which must answer 400 to an unsigned request.
- `health` alerts when the oldest unprocessed inbox event or job is older than 15 min.

**Left open:** what the Customer area holds and what its pages say (map fog "Contents of the Customer area"); which mails exist (fog "Transactional mail"); firewall and internal networks ([Decide the network layout](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/69)).

## Question

comments.body: Input from [Decide Subscription lifecycle](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/38): Backup needs a signed-in Admin, but the Customer may not be one. Before an automatic closing, a Customer who is not an Admin cannot secure the data.

body:
## Question

What are the states of a Subscription and their effect on the Family: trial, trial end, active, payment failure, lock, cancellation, deletion? How do they map to the existing closing and grace period?

comments.body: Input from [Decide registration flow](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/37): trial is 2 weeks with payment method at the start and converts automatically; no pilot. Withdrawal and cancellation during the trial belong here.

**Decision: Subscription lifecycle**

- **Trial:** Stripe's native trial, 2 weeks. One paid contract from the order, first 2 weeks free, so one withdrawal period from the order. The order page states first charge date and amount. No reminder mail before the first charge.
- **Cancel:** the Family keeps running until the trial or billing period ends, then closing. No charge when cancelled in the trial.
- **Yearly after year one:** keeps charging yearly, cancellable any time with one month's notice, unused part refunded (§ 309 Nr. 9).
- **Payment failure (including first charge):** days 0-7 past due, with retries, mails and full use. Days 7-14 Payment lock. Day 14 Subscription cancelled, closing starts.
- **Payment lock:** all members see an overdue page, workers pause, Customer can update payment, Admins can download a Backup. Payment unlocks at once.
- **Closing:** one path for every end: lock at once, 7-day grace, deletion (day 21 for non-payment). The decision in #20 stands: grace is for Operator undo on request only, no self-service return. The closing mail names contact and deletion date.
- **Backup before automatic closing:** possible during normal use until period end and during Payment lock, with reminder mails. Grace stays closed.
- **Withdrawal:** closing at once, Backup offered in the withdraw flow. Refund the amount paid minus pro-rata Wertersatz for paid days only.
- **Chargeback:** straight to Payment lock, then as day 7 of payment failure; unlock if won.
- **Operator termination:** cancels the Subscription and starts closing; mail states the reason.
- **Tariff switch:** takes effect at end of the billing period, no proration; at once during the trial.

Lawyer review: contract and order wording, yearly renewal, Wertersatz, termination clause.
Consequences: Payment lock and Backup access during it are new requirements on the app. A Customer who is not an Admin cannot download a Backup: goes to Decide Customer succession. `GLOSSARY.md` gained Payment lock.

title: Decide Subscription lifecycle

body:
## Question

What are the steps from landing page to first sign-in: invitation link for the pilot, Identity Provider, acceptance of terms, provisioning trigger, failure and retry, abuse protection, and the switch to open registration?

comments.body:
**Decision: registration flow**

Steps: landing page → choose tariff (monthly or yearly) → sign-in → confirm mail address → order page (mandatory information, terms, payment method, order button) → provisioning → app, where Onboarding runs.

- **No pilot, no invitation links.** Registration is open from launch, so billing and legal texts must be live first.
- **Identity Providers:** Google plus one Operator-run OIDC provider. No Microsoft, Apple or netID.
- **Operator-run provider:** Authentik, subject to the spike; fallback Ory Kratos + Hydra. Pocket ID rejected. Sign-in by mail link or code, repeatable; passkey offered, never forced; no passwords. Mail sign-in is also the recovery path. Open signups stay off; our registration creates users through the API.
- **Accepted risk:** sign-in is as strong as the mailbox; a mail outage blocks users without a passkey.
- **Mail address:** prefilled from the claim, confirmed by the Customer, verified by code or link before ordering. Same path for all providers.
- **Trial:** 2 weeks with payment method taken at the start; turns into the Subscription automatically. Replaces trial without a payment method. §§ 312j and 312k buttons needed from day 1; button label for lawyer review.
- **Acceptance:** one unticked checkbox for terms, plus 18+ and consumer confirmation; privacy notice linked; version and timestamp stored.
- **Provisioning:** queued job triggered by Stripe's webhook for the created Subscription in trial. Waiting page polls; automatic retries with backoff, then Operator alert and a "we'll mail you" page. On final failure the Operator cancels the Subscription before any charge. Sign-in resumes where registration stopped.
- **Already mapped person:** detected by `iss`+`sub` after sign-in and sent to their Family. A second provider account counts as another person; a verified mail address already used by a Customer is blocked.
- **Abuse:** one trial per card fingerprint and per verified mail address, otherwise the order starts without trial. Rate limits per IP, daily provisioning cap with Operator alert. No CAPTCHA.
- **Abandoned registrations:** deleted after 30 days.

title: Decide registration flow

body:
## Question

Which payment provider does the service use, and is it a Merchant of Record?

comments.body:
**Decision: Stripe Billing + Stripe Tax. No Merchant of Record. The Operator is the merchant.**

Why: an MoR was first preferred for least work, but deeper research ([Paddle](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/42), [German providers](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/43)) showed unresolved blockers before the first sale: yearly renewal vs § 309 Nr. 9 BGB, the § 312j order button, prices under $10, plus contract rework. As own merchant, terms and order path are under our control, fees are about half, and `GLOSSARY.md` stays valid.

Accepted cost: VAT returns, OSS once above EUR 10,000 cross-border B2C, disputes, buyer support, bookkeeping. Small at low revenue.

Consequences:
- Customer and Subscription definitions unchanged.
- Candidate set closed; Mollie and others not compared.

## Question

Which Identity Providers should hosted sign-in offer in the EU (Google, Apple, Microsoft, others)? Cover `email_verified` behaviour, cost, setup effort, privacy implications, and the options for people without such an account given that hosted has no password sign-in.

comments.body:
## Resolution

Findings: `docs/research/identity-providers.md` (untracked for now; the repo has no commits).

- **Key:** only `iss`+`sub` is stable. Apple and Microsoft `sub` are pairwise, so mappings depend on the client registration.
- **`email_verified`:** not comparable across providers. Google is authoritative only for Gmail and Workspace. Microsoft documents no such claim and says `email` isn't guaranteed correct. Apple lists it, but may yield a relay address (its wording confirmed only via forum quotes). So the "verified email" half of the register mapping (#20) is weak.
- **Cost/effort:** Google: no fee found, brand verification needs public homepage + privacy policy. Apple: 99 USD/year, App ID + Services ID, relay mail setup (SPF/DKIM). Microsoft: publisher verification free and apparently not needed for sign-in only.
- **No such account:** options are requiring one, netID (portal free, claims unverified), or an Operator-run standalone OIDC provider with passkeys (must not broker, per #20). EUDI Wallet acceptance isn't mandatory for us (Art. 5f(2) exempts micro/small enterprises).
- **Privacy:** provider sees each sign-in; US transfer rests on the DPF, appeal C-703/25 P registered. Needs legal review.

No decision made; open checks are listed at the end of the note.

body:
## Question

What must a German Einzelunternehmer provide when selling a B2C Subscription in the EU? Cover Widerruf, Kündigungsbutton, Impressum, AGB, privacy notice, processing of family and children's data, AVV relevance, trial-to-paid rules, and which duties a Merchant of Record takes over. Not legal advice; flag points for review.

comments.body:
Resolved. Findings: `docs/research/legal-duties-b2c-eu.md` (untracked in repo; not legal advice, review list included).

Gist:
- Service is most likely a digitale Dienstleistung: withdrawal survives use and ends only on full performance; early start gives pro-rata Wertersatz.
- Three buttons: `zahlungspflichtig bestellen` (§ 312j; otherwise no contract), `Verträge hier kündigen` (§ 312k), `Vertrag widerrufen` (§ 356a, since 19 June 2026).
- Yearly tariff: renewal for another fixed year is invalid in AGB (§ 309 Nr. 9); after year one only indefinite, cancellable any time with max one month's notice.
- Trial: paid contract as a new active order step avoids the C-565/22 question.
- Children/family: Operator bound by GDPR despite the household exemption; Art. 14 info, Art. 9 data in entries, DPIA likely.
- AVV: none with household Customer (to confirm); needed with hosting, LLM, OCR, mail vendors; Paddle-type MoR is an independent controller.
- MoR (Paddle checked only) takes sale, VAT, invoices, payment, refunds, checkout-side withdrawal. Impressum, privacy, conformity, change notices, support stay with seller.
- Extra: Data Act switching and AI Act Art. 50 may apply; BFSG exempt as microenterprise.

Flagged for lawyer: classification, yearly renewal, trial, controller role, MoR withdrawal mismatch, Data/AI Act. Not verified: current Muster-Widerrufsbelehrung.

body:
## Question

Which providers fit an Einzelunternehmer (no Kleinunternehmer) selling a B2C Subscription across the EU? Compare Merchant of Record options with Stripe Billing on: fees, EU VAT handling, invoices, trial without payment method, dunning (retries, reminder mails), Customer portal, webhooks, cancellation button support, payout and accounting effort.

comments.body:
Resolved. Findings: `docs/research/payment-providers.md` (untracked for now; the repo has no commits yet). Comparison only, no decision.

- **Stripe Billing + Tax**: cheapest (about 3.2% on an illustrative €50 yearly charge, 7.7% on €5 monthly). Only provider with full trial without payment method (GA). Maintainer stays merchant: OSS and VAT returns, disputes and support remain. Stripe does not file for a German seller.
- **MoR** (Paddle, Stripe Managed Payments, Lemon Squeezy, Polar): VAT and most accounting go away, at about 6-7.5% on €50 and 11-17% on €5.
- **Trial without payment method**: Paddle has early access only (API only, no reminders, no portal support). Polar's built-in trial collects payment info. Lemon Squeezy's guide tracks it in the app. Managed Payments documents no such flow. An app-side trial with checkout at conversion works with all of them.
- **§ 312k BGB**: no provider covers it out of the box. Own button and confirmation page needed in every case.
- **Glossary conflict**: under an MoR the sale is with the MoR, while `GLOSSARY.md` makes the Customer the Operator's contract partner. Needs legal review.
- **Portal**: Stripe and Paddle cover payment details, invoices and cancellation, which informs the Customer area.

Open: Managed Payments cardless trial (sandbox test), MoR product acceptance, German tax and legal points marked in the file. Lemon Squeezy and Polar details partly unverified.

Every decision for the public entry point of the hosted service is made (landing page, registration, billing, Customer area, legal texts, transactional mail), so the work can be handed off as implementable issues in this repo. This map plans only; it builds nothing.

## Notes

- Fresh effort announced as out of scope in map #1; its decisions stand. In particular: hosted sign-in only through Operator-configured Identity Providers (no passwords), one Family per person, provisioning per [Provision and remove a database per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/26), closing locks at once with a 7-day grace period, Onboarding runs in the app after first sign-in.

- Seller: the maintainer as Einzelunternehmer, not a Kleinunternehmer (§ 19 UStG does not apply). Market: EU, German and English.
- Model: 2-week trial with payment method taken at the start, converting to the Subscription. One tariff, monthly and yearly; price set after usage measurements.
- No pilot: registration opens at launch, with billing and legal texts live.
- Contract partner is the **Customer**, the person who registers (see `GLOSSARY.md`).
- No lawyer review: the maintainer writes legal wording to best knowledge, conservative and close to the statute; "lawyer review" in earlier decisions means this.
- Language: English in tickets; domain terms untranslated. Skills: `grilling` + `domain-modeling` for decisions.

## Decisions so far

- [Compare payment providers](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/33): Stripe Billing + Tax is cheapest with full cardless trial but leaves VAT filing with the maintainer; MoRs remove VAT work at about double cost or more and conflict with the Customer contract definition; own § 312k button needed either way.
- [Research Identity Providers for hosted sign-in](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/35): only iss+sub is a stable key; email_verified is not comparable across Google, Apple, Microsoft; no-account options are netID or an Operator-run passkey OIDC provider (see docs/research/identity-providers.md).
- [Research legal duties for selling a B2C subscription in the EU](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/34): Three buttons required (order, cancel, withdraw); withdrawal survives use with pro-rata Wertersatz; yearly tariff cannot renew for a fixed year (§ 309 Nr. 9); paid start as active order step; MoR takes sale, VAT, refunds but not Impressum, privacy, conformity; lawyer review list in `docs/research/legal-duties-b2c-eu.md`.
- [Research Paddle as Merchant of Record in depth](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/42): No hard disqualifier; open blockers are yearly renewal vs § 309 Nr. 9, German order button label, bespoke pricing under $10; about 18% of net on €5, 7% on €50; Paddle sells, Operator supplies under separate agreement; no SEPA debit; app-side trial fits (see docs/research/paddle.md).
- [Research German Merchant of Record providers](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/43): Digistore24, ablefy, CopeCart, affilicon, Cleverbridge are real German-law resellers, but none clearly beats Paddle on least work: Digistore24 and affilicon ease § 309 Nr. 9 on paper, yet Digistore24's order button was held unlawful (LG Hildesheim 11 O 5/25), fees on €5 are about double, integration thinner; see docs/research/german-mor-providers.md.
- [Decide payment provider](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/36): Stripe Billing + Tax, no Merchant of Record; Operator is merchant, glossary stays, VAT work accepted.
- [Research Operator-run OIDC provider without forced passkeys](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/44): Pocket ID out; with mail code and no passwords only Authentik and self-hosted Ory Kratos + Hydra qualify on docs, untested (see docs/research/operator-oidc-provider.md).
- [Decide registration flow](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/37): No pilot; tariff, sign-in (Google or Authentik with mail code, passkey optional), mail check, order with card, then provisioning by Stripe webhook; one trial per card and mail.
- [Decide Subscription lifecycle](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/38): Stripe trial inside one contract from the order; failure: 7 days full use, 7 days Payment lock, then closing; every end uses closing with Operator-only grace; yearly continues cancellable with refund; no pre-charge reminder.
- [Decide Customer succession](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/39): Customer is always an Admin, protected from demotion and removal, so can always take a Backup.
- [Prototype landing page](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/41): Design accepted: scrollytelling page built from the family-agenda landing page with its design system, static in `site/` (German at the root, English under `en/`, on branch `claude/cloud-product-scrollytelling-1ce8b7`); six steps from scattered Sources to one Agenda, then Sources (no Messengers), data with Operator access stated openly, one tariff with trial conversion and payment method at the start, legal footer; still placeholders: price, targets of `/register` and the legal links, hosting and LLM claims pending [#62](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/62).
- [Test Authentik for mail sign-in](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/45): Authentik 2026.8.5 passes all checks (API users, repeated mail code and link without passwords, optional passkey, two unlicensed replicas, scanner-safe links via Continue step); before production remove the stock password flow, check signups off, test OIDC claims (see spikes/authentik-mail-signin/README.md).
- [Decide architecture of the private site](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/40): private `site` service (Hono + htmx) on the apex with `/register`, `/account`, `/stripe/webhook`, own `site` DB; internal `billing-worker` alone holds key file and CREATEDB, processes webhook inbox, provisioning, lifecycle and daily reconcile; Customer stays on landing with App + Account links, others go to the app; cancel/withdraw public and in Account.
- [Research Stripe Checkout and Customer Portal against the German button and cancellation duties](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/72): hosted Checkout button fixed to "Subscribe/Buy", so `site` builds own order page with Checkout Sessions `ui_mode: elements` (Payment Element, own "zahlungspflichtig bestellen" button, Stripe Tax); Portal only for payment method, invoices, tariff switch, its cancel disabled in favour of own § 312k page; refunds via API (see docs/research/stripe-hosted-pages.md on branch research/stripe-hosted-pages).
- [Decide order page](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/73): one own page under `/register` (tariff switch, name, EU country dropdown, Payment Element, two checkboxes, highlighted summary, button "Zahlungspflichtig bestellen"); one gross price EU-wide, EU only, payment methods set in the Stripe dashboard; used mail shows no trial up front, used card is checked after the click and the order cancelled uncharged; wording fixed in the issue.

## Not yet specified

- VAT and invoice handling: who files, German invoice content (tax adviser).
- Price and usage quotas (LLM, OCR): needs usage measurements.
- Legal text package: how the texts get written and maintained.

## Out of scope

- Marketing and SEO beyond the landing page.
- Operating the service (infrastructure, monitoring): tracked in [Run the hosted multi-Family service](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/24).
- Customer succession ([Decide Customer succession](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/39)): hand-over, Customer leaving, death or unreachability, notices to other Admins; not needed for launch.

Cost input from [Decide the cost model per Family](https://github.com/artkoenig/family-agenda-cloud/issues/60), for the price decision on this map:

- Cost per Family: **~1.25 EUR a month**, flat across scale (~1.00 of inference, ~0.20 of infrastructure). Fixed cost ~26 EUR a month at 100 Families, ~178 at 1000.

body:
## Question

How are the Family keys and the Family data protected so that one stolen secret (e.g. the operator key) does not expose every Family, and how does encryption of data at rest work **self-hosted as well as hosted**?

## Facts (main @ 57b7351)

- The master key protects only **credentials** (`EnvelopeSecretStore`: IMAP passwords, WebUntis secret, ICS URLs, LLM and OIDC client secrets) and, per "Decide Agenda link format", derives the Agenda link HMAC. **Messages, Items and blobs are stored unencrypted** in Postgres and the blob store.
- "Decide multi-family Instances in the public image" wraps each Family's master key with an operator key read from env/Docker secret; "Decide Recovery Kit in hosted operation" keeps it out of databases and backups.
- Risk today: database/backup access alone exposes all messages; together with the operator key also all credentials (live mailbox access).
- Fundamental limit: no end-to-end encryption with Family-only keys, since the worker polls Sources and calls the LLM with nobody signed in; the server must be able to decrypt.

## Requirement (maintainer, 2026-11-07)

- Encryption of data **must also work self-hosted**, not only in the cloud.

## Options to grill

1. **Operator key in a KMS / Vault** (e.g. OpenBao/Vault transit, or an EU cloud KMS) instead of env: the key never leaves; containers only unwrap single Family keys via API, with audit log, policies, maybe rate limits. Self-hosted: the file master key stays, or an optional Vault adapter?
2. **Data at rest:** app-level encryption of messages/attachments/Items with the Family key (works self-hosted without extra infrastructure, also protects dumps and backups) vs. storage-level encryption (encrypted volumes, S3 server-side encryption, encrypted backups), which only protects against stolen disks/backups. Cost of app-level encryption: no SQL search/filter over encrypted columns, key needed for every read, migration of existing data.
3. **Key separation:** derive separate keys from the master key (credentials, data, Agenda links), so `api` serving Agenda pages holds only what it needs; credentials decrypted only by the worker and the Source setup.
4. **OAuth instead of passwords** for mail providers that support it (Gmail, Outlook): revocable, limited tokens. Possibly its own ticket for the IMAP Source.
5. Key rotation (operator key, Family keys) and what it means for Agenda links (HMAC changes with the key) and the Recovery Kit.

Affects: "Decide multi-family Instances in the public image", "Decide Recovery Kit in hosted operation", "Decide Agenda link format", "Decide Backup format, export and restore in the app".

comments.body:
## Resolution

**Data at rest, app-level, self-hosted and hosted alike**
- **Encrypted:** all content — every free text that Sources deliver or Admins enter: `source_record` sender, subject, body, `stated`, link; Event title and location; Task title and `bring`; Family Member and Agenda names; and every blob (attachments, photos).
- **Plain:** structure — ids, times and dates, status, kinds, foreign keys — so the timeline and due queries keep working with their indexes. (No query searches text today.)
- **`external_id`** is stored as an HMAC with the Family's key: uniqueness stays, content (e.g. mail addresses in Message-IDs) is gone.
- **Where:** in the adapters — the Postgres repositories for columns, and a wrapper around every `BlobStore` (file and S3 alike). `domain` and `application` are unaware; port contracts unchanged. AES-256-GCM, random nonce per value.
- **Existing data:** a one-time, resumable in-app step encrypts existing rows and blobs in batches when a Family is opened (plain SQL cannot, the key lives only in the app); the Family is restricted until it finishes.

**Keys**
- The Family master key stays the single root (one Recovery Kit). HKDF derives separate keys for **credentials** (the existing `EnvelopeSecretStore`), **data**, and **Agenda links** (HMAC).
- All containers get all three for now (`api` also sets up Sources and needs credentials). Per-container distribution can come later without re-encrypting data.
- **Operator key (hosted):** new port `KeyWrapper` wraps/unwraps Family keys. Hosted: OpenBao/Vault transit — the operator key never leaves the vault, every unwrap is logged. A key from file/env only for development and tests. Self-hosted: the master key stays a file in its own volume; data encryption still protects dumps and backups, since the key is not part of them (ADR-0006).
- **Rotation:** operator key rotatable by re-wrapping all Family keys (Family keys, Agenda links and Recovery Kits unchanged). Family keys are not rotated; they change only on restore into another Instance (#18).

**Out of this map:** OAuth instead of passwords for mail providers (an IMAP Source feature).

Changes: "Decide multi-family Instances in the public image" (operator key from env → `KeyWrapper` with OpenBao/Vault transit), "Decide Recovery Kit in hosted operation" (operator key in the vault), "Decide Agenda link format" (HMAC with the derived link key).

body:
## Question

How do OCR models (tessdata, ADR-0012) work when containers are stateless and shared by many Families?

## Facts (main)

- Each boot runs `mkdir` on the tessdata directory and links the bundled models (`composition-root.ts`, `ocrModels.linkBundled()`).
- Admins can download further models from `tessdata_fast` into the `tessdata` volume; the Family's OCR languages are stored in the Family database.
- A download by one Family's Admin would land in a directory shared by every Family on that container, and other containers would not have it.

## Options to grill

- All offered languages baked into the image; no downloads when hosted (the language list is fixed by the operator).
- Models in shared object storage (S3), fetched on demand and cached per container.
- What the Admin area shows when hosted (choose languages only, no download).
- CPU cost of OCR in shared containers (limits per Family, queue).

comments.body:
## Resolution (maintainer, 2026-11-07)

**The Operator decides which OCR languages exist, the same for every Family on the Instance; the Family picks its OCR languages from those.** Self-hosted, the self-hoster is the Operator. No download and no deletion of models in the app any more; the OCR containers need no shared state.

**Two knobs, both the Operator's:**
- **Build argument `OCR_LANGUAGES`** in the public Dockerfile, default `deu eng` (plus `osd`). Models are fetched at build time from `tessdata_fast` at the pinned commit and checked against the shipped SHA-256 list. The public CI publishes the default image; the cloud builds **the same Dockerfile at the same release tag** with its own list (no own Dockerfile, no derived image). New containers are ready at once, nothing loads at start — this is how the hosted Instance scales.
- **Start parameter** (e.g. `OCR_EXTRA_LANGUAGES=fra,tur`): additional languages a container downloads at start — the self-hoster's way without an own build.
  - Same source, pinned commit and checksums; a file that does not match is discarded.
  - Target is the model directory; when a volume is mounted there (self-hosted today), files persist and a present file with a valid checksum is not downloaded again.
  - A failed download does not stop the start: the language counts as not available, and it is logged.
  - Optional Operator-set download base URL (mirror); the checksum list always applies.
  - Files placed there by hand still count (offline path); models downloaded by today's Instances keep working.

**Available OCR languages** = models in the image + models in the model directory.

**Admin area:** choose OCR languages from the available ones; no download button; note "further languages are provided by the Operator" (self-hosted: link to the docs of the start parameter). A chosen language that is not available is marked so; scanned attachments are then not read and their Message says why (no silent fallback, as today).

**CPU:** at most N Tesseract processes per worker container at once (Operator setting, default: number of CPUs); an Operator-set page limit per attachment, pages beyond it are not read and the Message says so. Fairness between Families comes from the due-index leases. Per-Family quotas belong to the private repo.

**ADR-0012 is revised** (it is `proposed`): models at build time from `tessdata_fast`, pinned commit and checksums; language list as build argument; start parameter and hand-placed files for self-hosters; in-app download and deletion removed. "All languages in the image" stays a rejected option with its reason (several hundred MB on every Instance, Raspberry Pi).

## Question

What does an Agenda link look like so that it identifies the Family (which database to open) and the Agenda, cannot be guessed, and works for the Agenda page, its ICS feed and photos? Same format self-hosted and hosted?

## Settled (maintainer, 2026-11-07, see "Decide multi-family Instances in the public image")

- One address for all Families; Agendas are told apart by the **path**.
- Links never expire, have no version or rotation; deleting the Agenda revokes them (amends ADR-0005).

## Options to grill

- `/a/<Family id>/<random secret>`: 128-bit secret stored hashed in the Family database; short (QR codes); Family id in clear so the server knows which database to open.
- Signed token (key per Family): no lookup needed to reject forgeries, but long and needs key handling.
- Self-hosted without a Family id in the path, or the same format everywhere?
- Migration of existing UUID links (`/agendas/:id`), and of ICS subscriptions already made with them.
- Leakage: logs, browser history, `Referer` (e.g. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on Agenda pages).

comments.body:
## Resolution

- **Format:** `/a/<Family id>/<Agenda id>.<secret>`, the same self-hosted and hosted (one code path). The Family id is random, generated once and stored in the Family database (also self-hosted).
- **Secret = HMAC(Family master key, Agenda id)**, truncated to 128 bits, base64url. Computed on demand, **nothing is stored**: no hash, no `SecretStore` entry, no new column. Opening: read the Agenda id, recompute, compare in constant time; Agenda must still exist. The Admin area recomputes the link (and QR code) whenever needed. A database dump reveals no link, since computing it needs the master key, which is never in Postgres.
- **Revocation:** deleting the Agenda. No expiry, no version, no rotation (amends ADR-0005). The links of an Instance change only when its master key changes (restore into another Instance, #18), where the address changes anyway.
- **Under the link:** everything that hangs off `/agendas/<uuid>` today: page, `/days`, `/activity`, `/tasks/...`, `/feed.ics`, `/manifest.webmanifest`; **new:** `/photos/<member>`, only for Family Members this Agenda shows. `/family-members/<id>/photo` remains for signed-in Admins only (settles the review finding on unauthenticated photos).
- **Old UUID links** stop working, no redirect (it would reveal the secret to anyone knowing the UUID). Acceptable at 0.1.x; release notes tell Families to re-copy links, re-add ICS subscriptions and reinstall home-screen apps.
- **Leakage:** Agenda responses send `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (external links already use `rel="noreferrer"`); the secret segment is masked wherever paths are logged; docs note it for operators' own reverse proxies.

body:
## Question

How does the **public image** serve many Families from stateless, horizontally scalable `api` and `worker` containers, each Family with its own database, while self-hosting runs the same image with one container of each kind and one Family?

## Settled by the maintainer (2026-11-07)

- **One image for both.** The cloud runs the public image (`ghcr.io/artkoenig/family-agenda`), not a derived private image. Containers are stateless and run in parallel; only the database is bound to a Family. Self-hosting: one `api`, one `worker`, one Family.
- **Which Family a request belongs to:**
  - signed in (hosted): from the OIDC token (a Family claim), verified server-side; never from a plain cookie or header.
  - Agendas, their ICS feed and photos (no sign-in): from the **Agenda link**, which identifies Family and Agenda and cannot be guessed (signed token or random secret; to decide here). It replaces today's bare UUID.
  - worker: no request; it goes through the Families that have work due.
- **Agenda links never expire and have no version or rotation.** An Admin revokes a link by deleting the Agenda. This amends ADR-0005 (which asked for rotatable Agenda Links).
- The private repo shrinks to landing page, registration, provisioning (writing the Family claim at the Identity Provider), billing, operations.

## To decide here

- Family register: where (control database vs config), what it holds (database, key reference), one entry from `DATABASE_URL` when self-hosted.
- Agenda link format: signed token (key per Family) vs random secret stored hashed; length (QR codes), leakage in logs/history/Referer.
- Worker across containers: how Families are picked (due index), and a database lock so two workers never poll the same Family/Source at once (today only the in-memory `polling ??=` guards it); in-memory values (`lastPurgeAt`, Recovery Kit `confirmed`) move to the database or are made harmless.
- Stateless containers: blobs to S3, master key per Family from KMS, tessdata in the image; file adapters stay for self-hosting.
- A person in several Families (e.g. separated parents): list claim and a Family switcher, or one Family per person.
- Instance lifecycle in a shared process: open/close per request or pooled (connections per database).

## Reopens

- "Decide ADR: The Instance is embeddable (ADR 0.3)": the public code now knows several Families per process.
- "Decide HTTP app without own server (1.4)": routing by Family moves into the public code; open Agenda access by UUID is replaced by Agenda links.
- "Decide Composition Root as library (1.1)": adapters are still injected, but by the public image's own multi-family wiring.
- Fog "Agenda link rotation/revocation" on the map: settled as above.

comments.body:
## Round 1 answers (maintainer)

- **Q1 address:** one address for all Families. Agendas are told apart by the path; signed-in requests by token/session (or path, to settle in round 2).
- **Q2 OIDC:** hosted additionally supports third-party Identity Providers such as Google (follow-up: where the Family comes from, since Google tokens carry no Family claim).
- **Q3 session cookie** `<Family id>.<session token>`, session row stays in the Family database: no objection.
- **Q4 register** as a port (single Family from `DATABASE_URL` self-hosted; control database via `CONTROL_DATABASE_URL` hosted): no objection.
- **Q5 Agenda link format:** split out to "Decide Agenda link format" (#21).
- **Q6 workers** share work through a due index in the control database (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, lease) plus an advisory lock per Family database; new work sets the Family due now: no objection.
- **Q7 in-memory values:** explanation requested (round 2).
- **Q8:** S3 blob adapter and per-Family master key wrapped by an operator key: no objection. **OCR** split out to "Decide OCR models in hosted operation" (#22).
- **Q9 a person in several Families:** out of scope.
- **Q10 open Instances per container:** explanation requested (round 2).

## Resolution

**Addressing**
- One address for all Families (`app.<domain>`), no subdomains. Admin paths stay `/admin/...` everywhere; the Family of a signed-in request comes from the session. Agendas carry the Family in the path (format: "Decide Agenda link format", #21).
- **Session cookie** `<Family id>.<session token>`; the session row stays in the Family database (token hashed, as today). A changed Family id finds no session in the other database, so no signature is needed. Self-hosted: no Family id, cookie as today.

**Sign-in when hosted**
- The operator configures Identity Providers through the image's configuration (env), including third-party ones such as Google. The Family database's `identity_provider` row and its Admin page are unused when hosted; no password sign-in when hosted. Self-hosted unchanged.
- **Identity → Family** mapping lives in the register: (issuer, subject / verified email) → Family. Provisioning writes the first Admin; creating an Admin in the Admin area also writes the mapping. No broker IdP.
- A person in several Families: **out of scope**; one Family per person.

**Family register**
- A port in the public code. Self-hosted: exactly one Family from `DATABASE_URL`, no table. Hosted: a control database (`CONTROL_DATABASE_URL`, switches the hosted mode on) with Family id → database, wrapped Family key, status, due time. Family ids are random, not speaking. Provisioning (private repo) creates Families.

**Workers**
- Due index in the control database: a worker claims due Families with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a lease, runs `dueWork.run()`, writes back `nextDueAt()`. An advisory lock per Family database as second guard (the only guard self-hosted). New work (e.g. a Source added) sets the Family due now; this settles "waking the worker".
- `dueWork` is polling and extraction only; **retention moves to cleanup** (changes "Decide worker as due-work functions (1.3)").

**Cleanup**
- Own container kind `cleanup` (image start command), running e.g. daily over all Families in the register: (1) retention: messages older than X or no longer needed, (2) secret sweep, (3) final deletion of Families whose closing is due. Self-hosted: the same code as a daily timer inside the worker container, no extra container.
- **X** is set by the operator in the image configuration (default 180 days, today's `messageRetentionDays`), not per Family, and published in the privacy policy (GDPR art. 5 (1)(e), art. 13 (2)(a)). No `lastPurgeAt` per Family.
- **Close Family** (hosted only): an Admin requests it with confirmation; a Backup download is offered first; the Family is locked at once (no sign-in, Agenda links invalid, no polling); after a grace period (e.g. 14 days) cleanup deletes the Family database, its blob prefix, its key, the register entry and its identity mappings. Grace period stated in the privacy policy.
- Operator backups drop closed Families as they expire (e.g. 30 days, stated in the privacy policy); the backup system is private-repo work.

**Stateless containers**
- S3-compatible `BlobStore` adapter with a prefix per Family; files stay the default.
- Each Family's master key is stored in the register, wrapped by an operator key (key encryption key) the image reads from env or a Docker secret; a vendor KMS can come later as another adapter. OCR models: "Decide OCR models in hosted operation" (#22).
- The Recovery Kit `confirmed` cache is harmless (only changes from no to yes); new in-memory state is barred by the 1.9 lint rule.

**Open Instances per container**
- LRU of open Instances (connection + wired use cases), each with a small pool (1–2 connections), closed after an idle time (e.g. 5 min); maximum count and idle time configurable; concurrent requests for one Family open it once (single-flight). Self-hosted: the one Instance stays open.

The operator key is no longer read from env/Docker secret in production: a `KeyWrapper` port wraps/unwraps Family keys, hosted via OpenBao/Vault transit (the key never leaves the vault, every unwrap is logged); file/env only for development and tests. ## Question

What does the onboarding that replaces `/setup` look like, and how is the LLM endpoint either configured by the Family (self-hosted) or set by the embedder without the Family seeing it (hosted)? Public-repo feature.

## Settled by the maintainer

- There is an onboarding, from which a Family can also start by restoring a Backup (see the Backup ticket).
- **Self-hosted:** the LLM can be configured in the onboarding, and changed later in the Admin area.
- **Hosted:** the LLM is set by the embedder; the Family does not see it and cannot change it.
- Restoring needs a signed-in Admin; also during onboarding.

## Facts from the code (main @ 83a960d)

- `/setup` creates the first Admin and is open until one exists (`apps/api/src/http/app.tsx:240-274`).
- `extractPending()` returns early when no `llm_endpoint` row exists (`packages/application/src/extraction.ts:166-167`), and `ExtractionRequest` always carries `endpoint` (`ports.ts:740`). An injected `Extractor` alone (decision in #7) therefore never runs on a hosted Instance.

## Proposal to grill

**Flow (self-hosted):** language → first Admin (password or Identity Provider) → signed in → choose "Start new" or "Restore from Backup" → Recovery Kit (new only) → LLM endpoint (skippable, only if not set by the embedder; a reminder stays in the Admin area).

**Flow (hosted):** landing page registers and the embedder creates the Admin (#7) → Admin signs in → same onboarding, without the LLM step.

**LLM port:** a "which endpoint applies" lookup replaces direct reads of the `llm_endpoint` row in extraction, `nextDueAt()` and the Admin area.
- Self-hosted default: the stored row, editable.
- Embedder-set (`Adapters`, e.g. `llm: { managed: endpoint }`): no row, the onboarding step and the Admin page are absent (routes 404), a restored Backup's endpoint and its secret are discarded.
- Also useful for self-hosters who fix the LLM centrally.

- **Contents:** logical export of the Family database, the blobs, the migration version; secrets as stored (wrapped with the source Instance's master key). Encrypted with a key derived from the Recovery Kit (ADR-0006).

## Resolution (maintainer, 2026-11-07)

Builds on the earlier decision in this ticket (restoring Admin kept). Public-repo feature; an ADR is drafted when the work is handed off.

**Key: the Family takes over the Backup's master key.** Restore needs the Recovery Kit of the source; the Family adopts that master key (hosted: wrapped via `KeyWrapper`). Data, blobs, credentials, `external_id` HMACs and Agenda-link tokens stay valid as stored; nothing is re-keyed. The Family's previous Recovery Kit becomes invalid, and the UI says so. This is not a rotation: the whole Family, key included, is replaced. (Re-keying everything under the target key was rejected: a run over all columns and blobs that breaks when interrupted.)

**Format:** an image of all Family database tables as stored (content stays ciphertext), all blobs, and the migration version, written as one stream and encrypted as a whole with a backup key derived (HKDF) from the master key (AES-256-GCM in chunks), so the plain structure (times, statuses) is protected too. Older Backup → loaded at its version, then migrated; newer → refused (`NewerMigrationHistoryError`). No separate domain-level export format.

**Not included:** sessions; Matrix data (Matrix Sources come back Failing and need "Fix"; not restored at all when hosted); the LLM endpoint, **neither self-hosted nor hosted**. Messages beyond the retention period are removed by the cleanup worker after the restore.

**LLM endpoint on restore:** the target keeps its own endpoint. Without one (fresh Instance), the Admin sets it as in onboarding; until then Messages wait unprocessed.

**Size:** export and import stream, never all in memory. No limit self-hosted; hosted, the operator configures a maximum upload size.

**Closing a Family:** no sign-in after closing, so no download during the grace period. The closing dialog offers the Backup download as a step before the Family is locked; the Admin may skip it on purpose.

**Scope:** manual download only; nothing stored on the server. Scheduled Backups to own storage → out of scope for this map.

## Question

Signatures and semantics of `runDueWork(worker)`, `nextDueAt(): Date | null`, retention and secret-sweep as separate calls; how `main.ts` sleeps until due; behavior on clock changes and newly added work.

comments.body: Fact-check delta (see docs/research/public-repo-factcheck.md): Intervals confirmed (5 s poll, 5 s services, 1 h retention). Secret sweep runs only once at start; extraction runs inside the poll tick; due-ness comes from each source's last run, so `nextDueAt()` needs a new query.

## Resolution

- **API:** one unit `worker.dueWork` with `run(): Promise<DueWorkReport>` and `nextDueAt(): Promise<Date | null>`. `run()` does polling, then extraction, then retention if due (retention: `lastPurgeAt + 1 h`, kept in memory; a fresh Instance counts as never purged, so it is due at once). `nextDueAt()` is the minimum over polling (`lastRunAt + interval`), extraction (pending messages and an LLM endpoint: now) and retention. The single calls `pollDue`, `extractPending`, `purge` stay exported for tests and special cases.
- **Semantics:** `Date` when something is due (a past date means now); `null` means nothing is scheduled.
- **Sleeping:** `main.ts` sleeps until `min(nextDueAt, now + maxSleep)` with `maxSleep` = 15 s (was 5 s). The worker gets no signal about new work from the api process, hence the cap. No wake hook in the library; in hosted operation the gateway/scheduler wakes a Family on request (Phase 2).
- **Clock:** a `lastRunAt` in the future counts as due (in `isDue` and `nextDueAt` alike); forward jumps are caught by the cap. Test with the `Clock`.
- **Outside `run()`:** services reconciliation (`worker.services.reconcile()`, every 5 s in `main.ts`, switchable per Instance via 1.2) and the secret sweep (`worker.secretSweep.sweep()`, once at start) are lifecycle/cleanup, not due work.
- **Overlap and report:** `run()` guards itself; a second call while one runs returns the running promise. One `DueWorkReport` merges the poll and extraction reports; logging stays with the caller, with an exported helper `logDueWorkReport(report, log)`. No time or count budget per `run()`; fairness between Families is the Phase 2 scheduler's job.

## Review against the code (main @ 83a960d)

- ❌ **`nextDueAt()` loops hot when the endpoint fails.** Extraction counts as due while messages wait and an endpoint is set. When the endpoint is unreachable or refuses the key, messages stay pending (`packages/application/src/extraction.ts:160-178`), so `nextDueAt()` returns "now" forever: self-hosted the worker calls the LLM endpoint without pause (today the 5 s tick throttles it); hosted, every Family with a broken endpoint is always due. Needs a backoff, e.g. `lastExtractionFailureAt + backoff`.
- Note: today a future `lastRunAt` counts as **not** due (`packages/application/src/polling.ts:148`); the decision changes that behaviour deliberately; worth a test.

## Question

Shape of `bootApplication`/`bootWorker` taking injected adapters (DB connection, `SecretStore`, `BlobStore`, `Extractor`, `JobQueue`, `Clock`), the `selfHostedAdapters(config)` factory, and what is public API vs internal.

comments.body: Fact-check delta (see docs/research/public-repo-factcheck.md): `bootApplication` already accepts optional overrides (clock, secretStore, blobStore, extractor, textExtractor, identityProviderClient, tessdataCatalog, connectDatabase). `bootWorker` hard-wires `PgBossJobQueue(databaseUrl)`; `masterKeyFile` is required; password hasher, plugin dirs and Tesseract model dir are not injectable. `readConfig()` is called by entry points, not inside boot. Only `JobQueue.start/stop` are used anywhere.

## Resolution

- **Signature:** `bootApplication(config, adapters)` and `bootWorker(config, adapters)` with a required, complete `Adapters` object; the boot functions never build defaults themselves. `selfHostedAdapters(config)` returns today's defaults; `main.ts` wires both.
- **JobQueue:** injected as an adapter (pg-boss stays the default in `selfHostedAdapters`); the port is left unchanged until it has real consumers.
- **Newly injectable:** password hasher, OIDC identity-provider client, tessdata catalog, plugin sources. The master key becomes an optional value/provider in `Adapters` (self-hosting reads it from the file); without it the Recovery Kit is unavailable. Existing overrides (clock, secretStore, blobStore, extractor, textExtractor, connectDatabase) are folded into `Adapters`.
- **Config split:** `readConfig()` stays in the entry points. `ApplicationConfig` holds behavior settings only (no file paths, no `databaseUrl`); everything with I/O lives in `Adapters`.
- **Placement:** the composition root moves into its own package (e.g. `packages/composition`); `apps/api` and `apps/worker` become thin entry points.
- **Public API:** the package's exports are the library API (boot functions, `Adapters`, `selfHostedAdapters`, port types). Later guardrails (1.9) and publishing (1.7) hang off this boundary.
- **Open (fog):** Recovery Kit in hosted operation with a KMS-based `SecretStore`.

## Review against the code (main @ 83a960d)

- ❌ **Master key should be required, not optional.** `EnvelopeSecretStore` keeps secrets in the Family database, wrapped with the master key. A hosted Instance needs no separate KMS `SecretStore`: inject the per-Family master key (from KMS) instead of reading the file. Then the Recovery Kit stays and is the way back to self-hosting and the key for restoring Backups (#18). Proposal: `Adapters.masterKey` as a required value/provider; the file is the self-hosted provider.
- ⚠️ **pg-boss is started but unused.** `bootWorker` starts `PgBossJobQueue` (`apps/api/src/composition-root.ts:377`), and `send`/`work` are called nowhere. Each start creates a pg-boss schema, its own pool and maintenance timers in every Family database. Proposal: remove pg-boss and the `JobQueue` port instead of injecting it.
- ⚠️ **Time zone** defaults to the process's (`composition-root.ts:166`); it must be required per Instance when hosted.
- ⚠️ **tessdata:** each boot runs `mkdir` and `linkBundled()`; an Admin's OCR model download lands in the shared directory and affects every Family. Belongs to making tessdata injectable.
- ⚠️ **Cost per open:** `SourceRegistry.discover` (directory reads), `sourceTypes.start()`, `catalogues.start()` run on every boot; measure for the LRU pool.
- New: `Adapters` gets the LLM setting from #19 (stored vs embedder-set).

Reframed: hosted registration (landing page with OIDC login, billing) triggers provisioning and creation of the Instance's Admin, so setup is automated by the embedder through the library, not via CLI or web setup. The ticket title's "CLI" parts are dropped.
